name: the storage goes away from one machine and comes back
comments: server-host loses the shared storage for 40 seconds - the network drops what it sends there, as a
lost route does: nothing refuses, nothing answers. Its two nodes have to stop serving clients
once their leases run out, and serve again soon after the storage is back; the other machines
carry on. On the default test cluster of test_cluster.sh, run from client-host. The 'after' commands give the
route back whatever happened, so a failed run does not leave server-host without its storage.
cluster: node1@client-host node2@client-host node3@server-host node4@server-host node5@farm-host node6@farm-host

timeline.command: ssh server-host sudo -n iptables -I OUTPUT -p tcp -d farm-host --dport 6379 -j DROP

timeline.check: server-host refuses clients without its storage

timeline.command: ssh server-host 'while sudo -n iptables -D OUTPUT -p tcp -d farm-host --dport 6379 -j DROP 2>/dev/null; do :; done'

after: ssh server-host 'while sudo -n iptables -D OUTPUT -p tcp -d farm-host --dport 6379 -j DROP 2>/dev/null; do :; done'

checks.name: server-host refuses clients without its storage
